name: Mud Brown
lede: Mud Brown is a dark, olive-leaning brown, a descriptive everyday name that entered color lists only recently.

sections.title: The color of wet soil
sections.body:
Paterson defines mud as the color of wet soil and notes that it appears in Winifred Nicholson's *Chart of Colours* of 1944; mud brown he simply calls a dark brown [1]. Our library traces the specific name to a 2010 online color survey, the xkcd list, and to no earlier chart [2]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 would file this swatch as a "moderate olive brown" (block 95) at 3.9 CIEDE2000 units away, and the nearest name in our learning set is plain [[brown]], 9.8 away [2].

The darker end of the same family includes [[umber]] and [[mud]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color near it appears in 1,521 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, 6.4%, more often than 88% of the named colors, as photographed [3]. It most often plays a mid-tone, and it is most devoted to Paulus Potter, in 8 of his 28 works here [3]. It shares canvases with Muddy Brown and [[mustard-brown]] more than chance [3]. The hue of old varnish also browns paintings, so a match is a screen color and not a pigment [3]. In printed English the name peaks in the 2010s [4].
